<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Let me check the last transition to see exactly what changed
# Also check if any white dots are now at the same position as the player
seg = current_frame.segmentation

# Player position

for n in seg['nodes']:
    if n['color'] == 'O':
        # Get all cells in the player's boundary
        for b in n['boundary']:
            player_cells.add(tuple(b))
        # Also include interior cells
        rows = [b[0] for b in n['boundary']]
        cols = [b[1] for b in n['boundary']]
        min_r, max_r = min(rows), max(rows)
        min_c, max_c = min(cols), max(cols)
        for r in range(min_r, max_r+1):
            for c in range(min_c, max_c+1):
                player_cells.add((r, c))
        print(f"Player occupies: {sorted(player_cells)}")

# Check if any white dots overlap with player
print("\n=== White dots near player ===")
for n in seg['nodes']:
    if n['color'] == 'W' and n['pixels'] == 1:
        pos = n['boundary'][0]
        dist = min(abs(pos[0]-31), abs(pos[1]-23))
        print(f"  {pos}, dist_to_player_center={dist}")

# Let me try pressing RIGHT to see if player moves right (against the scroll)
# If RIGHT moves player right, then directional keys DO control movement
result = action(['RIGHT'])
seg2 = current_frame.segmentation
for n in seg2['nodes']:
    if n['color'] == 'O':
        print(f"\nAfter RIGHT: Player boundary={n['boundary']}")

# Compare with before RIGHT
print(f"Step: {current_frame.step}")

</function>
</tool_call>
